topic: How can frequency planning address interference between satellite uplinks and broadband power line communication systems?
consensus_response: Satellite uplink and power line communication system interference stems from shared frequency bands and limited bandwidth.  Frequency planning must consider modulation schemes' impact on interference, with higher modulation schemes increasing spectral density and potential for interference.  Dedicated frequency bands and exclusion zones are costly and complex but can mitigate interference.  Accurate propagation modeling and simulation tools are crucial for predicting and minimizing interference before deployment, reducing the need for expensive mitigation strategies later.
reference_context: Interference between satellite uplinks and power line communication systems arises from shared frequency bands and limited bandwidth.  Satellite uplinks suffer from line-of-sight limitations, leading to multipath fading and increased interference.  Power line communication faces similar challenges, requiring careful frequency planning and modulation scheme selection to minimize interference and optimize system performance.
